subject: CHS — Prepay structuring and invoice allocation
messages:
From: Caitlin Reyes <caitlin.reyes@columbiahealth.org>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@columbiahealth.org>, Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@columbiahealth.org>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: CHS terms — final commercial questions on prepay/term discounts

Thanks Kimberly — team has reviewed the SOW and the committed prepay pricing looks good. A couple of procurement / finance items before we sign:

- We need confirmation on how Redwood will invoice a multi-year prepay. Our fiscal year ends 2026-12-31; we prefer to split billing so FY26 shows only the portion applicable to that year.
- If Redwood invoices a single prepay now, will you provide an amortization schedule or accounting memo that we can attach to our AP records (ASC 606)?
- Also: can you confirm treatment of the term discount if the customer prepays for years 1–3 but the usage ramps? How should we reflect that in our PO/ledger?

We can move quickly once we have guidance and an invoice format we can process.

Thanks,
Caitlin
Procurement Manager
Columbia Health Systems

Attachment: CHS_SOW_v2.pdf (proposal SOW)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Caitlin Reyes <caitlin.reyes@columbiahealth.org>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: CHS terms — final commercial questions on prepay/term discounts

Hi Caitlin — great to hear the SOW looks good. Short answers up front, then proposed operational options: 

1) Invoicing options:
   - Option A (preferred for bookkeeping): Redwood issues separate invoices that map to each fiscal year portion (e.g., Invoice A: 2026 allocation, Invoice B: 2027 allocation).
   - Option B (if procurement requires a single prepay invoice): Redwood can issue a single prepayment invoice dated on the payment date and provide an amortization schedule (monthly or annual) that your AP/AR team can use to post deferred revenue.

2) Term discount / ramp: the commercial discount is applied to the committed prepay amount. For accounting, the discount is amortized across the service period consistent with ASC 606 — we can provide line-item allocation showing list price, discount, and net recognized per period.

3) What we need from CHS: preference for Option A vs B; PO instructions (single PO or multiple POs if splitting by year); billing contact and remit instructions for ACH/wire.

I’ve looped in Markus (Finance) to confirm the format of the amortization & invoice lines. I’m attaching our suggested invoice template for your AP team to review. If you prefer Option B, we will prepare the amortization schedule and a short accounting memo to support recognition.

Next step: if you confirm Option A (split invoices), we’ll issue two invoices timed to your year boundaries and include a memo for your records. If Option B, we’ll send the single invoice + amortization schedule for your accounting.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that’s easier.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: invoice_template_redwood.xlsx (stub)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Caitlin Reyes <caitlin.reyes@columbiahealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: CHS terms — final commercial questions on prepay/term discounts

Kimberly / Caitlin — quick finance note on implementation: 

- For Option A (split invoices) we need two separate invoice documents with explicit invoice dates and clearly separated line items (Year 1: service period MM/DD/YYYY - 12/31/2026; Year 2: 01/01/2027 - 12/31/2027). Each invoice should show the gross charge, applied term discount, and net amount. That makes it straightforward for CHS to recognize revenue in each fiscal year.

- For Option B (single prepay invoice): Redwood will create the invoice dated on payment receipt, but we will also produce an amortization schedule (CSV) and an accounting memo stating the revenue recognition approach and the allocation of the discount across the service months. This memo should be sufficient for CHS accounting to book a deferred revenue liability and amortize to revenue.

- Practical constraint: if CHS requires the cash to be received in FY26 (they indicated they may want that), Redwood can accept payment now and still supply the amortization schedule. We just need firm PO wording that references the amortization (so auditors have an audit trail).

I’m attaching our invoice template and a sample amortization file to illustrate. If CHS prefers Option B, please confirm the required amortization granularity (monthly vs annual). Monthly is preferred from our side for clean recognition.

-Markus
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference

Attachment: invoice_template_redwood.xlsx (sample)

From: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@columbiahealth.org>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Caitlin Reyes <caitlin.reyes@columbiahealth.org>, Procurement Team <procurement@columbiahealth.org>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: CHS terms — final commercial questions on prepay/term discounts

Thanks all. Procurement had a quick internal discussion — CHS will need the cash outlay to occur in FY26 (we have budget allocated this year), but our accounting team would prefer a single invoice process to minimize PO/header overhead. So: we want a single prepay invoice dated when payment is made (anticipated 10/05/2026) but require Redwood to provide an amortization schedule and a short accounting memo that we can attach to the PO to show how revenue will be recognized across 2026/2027/2028.

Also: please confirm that the term discount will be documented on the invoice (gross list price + discount line) so our auditors see the commercial rationale.

If Redwood can provide the single invoice + amortization + memo, procurement can issue the PO next week and we’ll route the DocuSign SOW.

Regards,
Andrew Miller
Sr. Director, Finance Operations
Columbia Health Systems

Andrew — thanks for the clarity, we can accommodate the single-invoice flow. Operational notes below: 

- Redwood will issue one prepay invoice dated on the payment date (we’ll use the invoice number format that includes the PO).
- We will attach a detailed amortization_schedule_proposal.csv that maps the prepay net amount across each accounting month of the service term. The CSV includes columns: period_start, period_end, gross_amount, discount_allocated, net_recognized.
- We will also include an accounting memo (short PDF) that describes the recognition method consistent with ASC 606 and shows the allocation of the term discount across the service months.

Next steps for us: Markus will finalize the amortization layout (we’ll provide monthly granularity by default). Marissa — can you confirm the DocuSign readiness once CHS returns the PO? Caitlin / Andrew — if you can approve the PO language to reference the amortization memo and specify payment expected by 2026-10-05, we’ll queue the single invoice on payment.

Estimated deliverables within 48 hours after PO confirmation: 1) Invoice (single prepay); 2) amortization CSV; 3) accounting memo PDF; 4) copy of invoice in SAP-friendly XLSX if required.

Best,
Kimberly
